title: Listening after renovation
bodyMd:
A fictional lecture room received sound-absorbing panels. Measurements showed a shorter reverberation time, and speech sounded clearer near the front. Students at the back still reported difficulty understanding lectures. Further observation found that a ventilation unit produced a steady noise near the rear seats.

The renovation had improved one aspect of the acoustic environment without resolving another. The engineers therefore avoided calling the panels ineffective, but also rejected the claim that the room’s listening problem was solved. They measured background noise separately and tested changes to the ventilation unit. The case illustrated why a successful intervention on one physical quantity may not deliver the whole experience that users need. A performance target can be met while the broader practical aim remains only partly achieved.
